lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: the structure of a deductive proof
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: the structure of a deductive proof

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

items.prompt: Third side is 18. Find the midsegment.

steps: Midsegment is half the third side.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: A proof concludes that base angles of an isosceles triangle are congruent, after constructing the bisector of the apex angle. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
choices: The base angles look equal in the diagram.
The bisector is perpendicular to the base by definition.
The two smaller triangles are congruent by SAS, so their corresponding base angles are congruent.
All triangles have congruent base angles.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 119°. Find the measure of the co-interior (same-side interior) angle.
In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure 53° and 51°. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: In a parallelogram, one angle measures 96°. Find the consecutive angle.
In a triangle, a segment joins the midpoints of two sides. The third side measures 18. Find the length of the midsegment and state its relationship to the third side.
choices: 9, and it is parallel to the third side
9, and it is perpendicular to the third side
18, and it is parallel to the third side
36, and it is parallel to the third side

items.prompt: A proof concludes that the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
choices: The diagonals are congruent, so they must bisect each other.
Alternate interior angles give two pairs of congruent angles, and the opposite sides are congruent, so the triangles formed are congruent by ASA.
Every quadrilateral has diagonals that bisect each other.
The diagonals are perpendicular, which forces bisection.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 110°. Find the measure of the co-interior (same-side interior) angle.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure 48° and 62°. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.
